item.title: Councillors give green light for proposed water-sports based facility at Ballybunion beach
item.description: Councillors have given the green light for a proposed water sports-based facility at Ballybunion beach. A vote was taken on the part 8 proposal at the Listowel Municipal District meeting, with it receiving unanimous support. The development will be located at Ballybunion South beach and includes a new public realm area adjacent to the facility, linking with the existing promenade. item.title: 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 22 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures provided by the Irish Nurses and Midwives’ Organisation. 13 people are on trolleys in UHK’s emergency department, while a further 9 patients are waiting on trolleys in wards elsewhere within the hospital. Advertisement Nationally, 602 people are waiting for beds in hospitals across the country today. University Hospital Limerick is the worst affected with 100 patients on trolleys. Advertisem

item.title: Conradh na Gaeilge calls for Irish language bonus marks to be included for 2026 Leaving Cert
item.description: Conradh na Gaeilge is urging the Department of Education to apply an Irish language marks bonus for students sitting the Leaving Cert in 2026. It follows calls by the Irish Second-Level Students' Union (ISSU) to ensure students within the Gaeltacht and Irish-speaking communities, are not disadvantaged in this year's Leaving Certificate. item.title: Kerry recognised by CDP as Global Leader in sustainability categories
item.description: Kerry Group has been honoured by CDP, the world’s leading environmental disclosure system. Kerry has been recognised as a global leader across categories such as climate change, forests and water security. The company received an ‘A’ rating for climate change leadership, placing it among the top 4 percent of businesses assessed by the CDP. Advertisement Group Head of Sustainability at Kerry, Juan Aguiriano, said the recognition from the CDP reflects Kerry’s continued commitment to sustainability

item.title: Jessie Buckley nominated for Best Actress Oscar
item.description: Killarney's Jessie Buckley has become the first Kerry woman to be nominated for a Best Actress Oscar. She was nominated for her role as Agnes Hathaway, the wife of William Shakespeare, in the drama Hamnet. While Jessie Buckley's co-star Paul Mescal missed out on a nod in the Best Supporting Actor category, the film is nominated for Best Adapted Screenplay, Costume Design, and Casting. item.title: Increased security presence at Shannon Airport ahead of expected Trump Air Force One stopover
item.description: There's an increased security presence at Shannon Airport ahead of an expected stopover by a plane carrying US President Donald Trump. It’s understood President Trump will not leave the plane, during what is expected to be a brief refuelling stop. Shannon Airport is operating as usual this evening, however there is a noticeable increase in security in the terminal and on the road into the airport. item.title: Young Kilcummin man who survived serious crash addresses road safety conference
item.description: A young Kilcummin man who had to learn how to walk again after a serious road crash has told TY students at a road safety conference about the dangers of the road. The AXA Roadsafe Roadshow 2026 took place at the INEC Killarney today, attended by around 1,900 students from secondary schools in Kerry.
